items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You know some of the greatest players, Zoot Sims and those fellas, are not as it’s called schooled in that

ctx.x: He plays them a little differently and it’s not like a symphonic trombonist who would play this measure and it would sound exactly the same every time. No. So I do notice that change now, which is I think good, not bad.

Well don’t let your teacher spoil you by making you do something that seems unnatural. You know some of the greatest players, Zoot Sims and those fellas, are not as it’s called schooled in that, but the ears are all-important.

You’ve got to listen all the time. When young players ask me, “What should I do,” just listen to good people all the time, and it doesn’t particularly matter. I even listen to some symphonic stuff. But just listen to good music all the time. And it’s certainly easy advice to follow.
